title: Derived scalar restriction and geometric pullback have invertible inverse mates
statement: For an arbitrary homomorphism a:A→B of discrete commutative rings and a scheme morphism f:X→Y [def-pc-scheme], on either small etale or pro-etale site use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The inverse scalar-adjunction mate of the canonical exact restriction/pullback square is invertible, with no coefficient flatness or boundedness assumption. The square is induced termwise by the canonical ordinary restriction/pullback square and transported through the exact geometric derived comparison. Scalar extension and restriction use [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; the geometric functors use [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The fixed scalar adjunctions and their normalized localization data are those of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility].

source.place: Finite rings paragraph, transport of scalar direct-image mates; canonical pullback/scalar and site comparison maps (Stacks 07A4, 0G7E, 09A6).

proof.text: The ordinary restriction/pullback square is conjugate to the pointwise coextension/direct-image identity. Iterated mates and the restriction/coextension triangle give an invertible ordinary scalar mate.

Pullback preserves flat-term K-flat resolutions, stalkwise on the etale site and by the local relation criterion under representably flat base change on the pro-etale site. Compute the derived mate using the normalized scalar adjunction units on these resolutions.
Transport invertibility through uniqueness of scalar left adjoints and the canonical exact inverse-image comparison. All transports are by natural isomorphisms.
